note: M28: dilemmas that follow from the crown's laws, faiths, lords and seasons, and the realm's demands for change. A dilemma fires when its `when` holds (laws signed, paths, faith levels, meters, season, war) and a fitting `place` is found; laws signed in the last half year weigh triple. Effects (fx): coin, love, fear, unrest (realm), townUnrest and prosperity (the place), opinion by group, devotion by faith, faith (shift in the place, points), loyalty (the lord named), sympathy (Scoia'tael). `next` raises a follow-up after some days. A demand asks for a law to be signed (or repealed) by a deadline: promise, refuse, or crush the agitators.
realmRequestsNote: M29 A: short requests a petty king sends the crown instead of seeking an audience (see diplomacy.json tiers). {ruler} and {realm} name the sender; realms limits a request to those realms. Effects as dilemmas, plus relation and trust (the sender's in the crown).

ships.title: {ruler} asks for ships against pirates
ships.text: Pirates out of the Skellige isles have burned two fishing villages on {realm}'s coast. {ruler} asks Vizima for hired ships and the coin to crew them.

choices.label: Pay for the ships
Send kind words and nothing else
Refuse: Temeria is no one's purse

grain.title: {ruler} asks for grain
grain.text: The harvest has failed in {realm}. {ruler} asks for wagons of grain from Temeria's granaries, to be repaid when the next harvest comes in.

choices.label: Send the grain
Sell it at the going price
Refuse

bandits.title: {ruler} complains of bandits from our side
bandits.text: Bandits cross from Temeria into {realm}, raid, and slip back over the border. {ruler} asks the crown to hang a few and pay for the damage.

choices.label: Pay for the damage
Promise to hunt them, and do nothing
Tell him to guard his own border

exiles.title: {ruler} asks us to hand over exiles
exiles.text: Some of {ruler}'s lords fled a quarrel at court and now sit in Temerian inns, drinking and plotting. {ruler} asks that they be sent home in chains.

choices.label: Hand them over
Give them a month to leave Temeria
Shelter them

toll.title: {ruler} asks for lower tolls
toll.text: {ruler} says Temeria's tolls strangle {realm}'s merchants, and asks that they be eased for a year.

choices.label: Ease them for a year
Ease them a little
Refuse

arbiter.title: {ruler} asks the crown to judge a border quarrel
arbiter.text: {ruler} and a neighbour quarrel over a mill and a ford. {ruler} asks Vizima to judge between them, and hopes for a kindly judgement.

choices.label: Judge in {ruler}'s favour
Judge fairly
Decline to meddle

dwarven_ore.title: The elders of Mahakam ask for a road mended
dwarven_ore.text: The road from Carreras to Mahakam's gates is falling apart, and dwarven carts break their axles on it. {ruler} asks the crown to mend it.

choices.label: Mend the road
Let the dwarves mend it, and pay half
Refuse

peasants_relief.title: The villages demand poor relief
peasants_relief.text: Hungry men have walked from the villages to the gates of Vizima. They ask the crown for bread in the lean months, and they say they will not go home without a promise.

peasants_granaries.title: The villages demand royal granaries
peasants_granaries.text: Last winter the grain ran out in March. The village elders ask the crown to keep its own stores against the hungry months.

burghers_markets.title: The burghers demand open markets
burghers_markets.text: The merchants of the towns complain of tolls at every bridge and ford. They want the roads open to trade, and they have stopped paying their dues on time to make the point.

burghers_charter.title: The towns demand a charter
burghers_charter.text: The guildmasters have drawn up a charter of the commons: the right of the towns to be heard before a tax is raised. They want the crown's seal on it.

lords_riders.title: The lords demand the king's riders
lords_riders.text: The great houses say the roads are not safe for their stewards or their rents. They want riders of the crown on every highway, and they want them before the next rising.

lords_knights.title: The lords demand royal knights
lords_knights.text: The younger sons of the great houses have trained at the academy and want spurs to show for it. Their fathers ask the crown to raise them as knights of the realm.

fire_restrictions.title: The Eternal Fire demands restrictions
fire_restrictions.text: The priests of the Fire preach that the non-humans in the towns are a rot in the realm. They demand that the crown bar them from the guilds, the councils and the walls after dark.

fire_inquisition.title: The Eternal Fire demands an inquisition
fire_inquisition.text: The Hierarch's men say restrictions are not enough. They want a holy office with the right to try witches, mages and heretics, and they want it sealed by the crown.

melitele_hospices.title: Melitele's priestesses ask for hospices
melitele_hospices.text: The priestesses of the Mother tend the sick on straw in the temple yards. They ask the crown to found hospices in every temple town, and the folk ask with them.

nonhumans_charter.title: The non-humans demand a charter
nonhumans_charter.text: Dwarven smiths and elven craftsmen pay the crown's taxes and are barred from its guilds. Their elders ask for a charter that names them subjects of the crown, with the rights of any other.

soldiers_standing.title: The captains demand standing companies
soldiers_standing.text: The captains say the levies break at the first charge and go home at harvest. They want paid companies who stay under arms in peace as in war.

peasants_repeal_long_hours.title: The labourers demand an end to long hours
peasants_repeal_long_hours.text: The mills and the mines work from dark to dark under the long hours law. The labourers have stopped work at three works and say they will not start again until the law is struck from the Book.

burghers_repeal_monopolies.title: The small traders demand an end to the monopolies
burghers_repeal_monopolies.text: Every craftsman outside the guilds is ruined or hanged. The small traders of the towns, more of them than the guildsmen, want the monopolies broken.

peasants_repeal_executions.title: The folk demand an end to public hangings
peasants_repeal_executions.text: There have been too many bodies on the gibbets. Mothers, priests and even some of the watch ask the crown to end the public hangings.

bread_thief.title: A boy to hang for bread
bread_thief.text: A boy of twelve is to hang at {place} for stealing a loaf. His mother waits at the gate with the whole street behind her. The baker says the law is the law.

choices.label: Hang him. The law is the law
Commute it to the stocks
Pardon him and fine the baker for his prices

bread_thief_after.title: The boy the crown pardoned
bread_thief_after.text: The boy pardoned at {place} has been seen carrying messages for the Scoia'tael in the woods. The watch says he knows their paths. He says the crown saved his life and he will tell the crown what he knows.

choices.label: Use him. He leads us to their camp
Let him be. He is a boy

gibbet_crowd.title: The crowd at the gallows
gibbet_crowd.text: A rebel the folk call a hero is to hang at {place}. The square is packed, and the watch fears the crowd will cut him down.

choices.label: Hang him with soldiers on every roof
Hang him at dawn, before the crowd gathers
Send him to the mines instead

curfew_wedding.title: A wedding after curfew
curfew_wedding.text: The watch at {place} broke up a wedding feast an hour past curfew. The bride's father struck a watchman. Half the street was at the wedding.

choices.label: The father is flogged. A curfew is a curfew
Fine him a crown and let it go
Discipline the watchmen instead

riders_excess.title: The king's riders burned a farm
riders_excess.text: Riders of the crown burned a farmstead near {place}, saying the family fed bandits. The neighbours swear the family fed no one but their own.

choices.label: Back the riders without question
Pay the family for the farm
Hang the rider who gave the order

assize_steward.title: The judge acquits a lord's steward
assize_steward.text: The travelling judge at {place} has acquitted {lord}'s steward of beating a tenant to death. Every man in the village saw it done.

choices.label: The verdict stands
Retry him before the crown's own court
Let it stand, but pay the widow from the treasury

assize_witch.title: A herbwife before the judge
assize_witch.text: The assize at {place} hears a case against a herbwife. The village says her potions killed a child; the child's mother says they saved two others.

choices.label: Hand her to the Fire's priests
Acquit her for want of proof
Exile her from the parish

pardon_brigand.title: A brigand begs pardon
pardon_brigand.text: A brigand captain who preyed on the roads near {place} offers to surrender with his men if the crown pardons them. They would serve in the levy.

choices.label: Pardon them and put them in the ranks
Promise pardon, then hang them
Refuse. Hunt them down

charter_tax.title: The charter tested
charter_tax.text: Under the charter of the commons the towns must be heard before a tax is raised. The treasury needs coin now; the guildmasters of {place} want to talk for a month first.

choices.label: Wait and hear them out
Raise the levy now and break the charter's spirit

beggars_flood.title: Beggars from abroad
beggars_flood.text: Word of the crown's bread has spread across the border. Beggars from Redania and Aedirn crowd the gates of {place} and the bread runs short for the town's own poor.

choices.label: Feed them all
Turn back the foreigners
Put them to work on the roads for their bread

hospice_plague.title: Fever in the hospice
hospice_plague.text: A fever has broken out in the hospice at {place}. The priestesses will not turn the sick away, and the townsfolk want the doors nailed shut with the sick inside.

choices.label: Keep the doors open and send physicians
Close the hospice until the fever passes
Nail the doors shut

feast_cost.title: The cost of the feast
feast_cost.text: The royal feast at {place} was a triumph. The steward now brings the bill: twice what was promised, and the wine merchants will not wait.

choices.label: Pay it in full
Pay half and let them sue

millwheel_arm.title: A millwheel takes an arm
millwheel_arm.text: Under the long hours law the mill at {place} grinds from dark to dark. A worker fell asleep at the wheel and lost his arm. The hands ask for one day of rest in seven.

choices.label: Grant them their day
Refuse. The work must go on
Pay the man a pension, nothing more

debtors_escape.title: Debtors run from the work gangs
debtors_escape.text: Twenty debtors labouring on the walls at {place} have broken their chains and fled to the woods. Their creditors want them hunted down.

choices.label: Hunt them down and add years to their debt
Let them go and forgive the debts

prison_gang_riot.title: The prison gang riots
prison_gang_riot.text: Convicts mending the road near {place} have killed a guard. The rest refuse to work until they are fed properly.

choices.label: Hang one in ten
Feed them and double the guard
Hang the killer, feed the rest

vivaldi_mint.title: The Vivaldi bank offers a loan
vivaldi_mint.text: Agents of the Vivaldi bank offer the crown a large loan at little interest. In return they want the running of the mint at {place} for five years.

choices.label: Accept. Coin now is coin now
Refuse. The mint is the crown's

merchant_smuggling.title: Chartered merchants caught smuggling
merchant_smuggling.text: A merchant house chartered by the crown has been smuggling fisstech through {place} under its seal. The other charter holders want it kept quiet.

choices.label: Revoke their charter publicly
Fine them heavily and keep it quiet
Take a share and look away

guild_forge.title: The guild burns a forge
guild_forge.text: Guildsmen at {place} have burned the forge of a smith who sold below the guild's price. He stands outside the castle with his burned hands wrapped in rags.

choices.label: Uphold the guild. He broke its rules
Hang the men who lit the fire
Rebuild his forge at the crown's cost

royal_mine_collapse.title: Men trapped in the crown's mine
royal_mine_collapse.text: A gallery has fallen in the royal mine near {place}. Eleven men are trapped, alive, behind the rock. Digging them out will stop the mine for a month.

choices.label: Dig them out, whatever it costs
Seal the gallery and dig elsewhere

granary_hoard.title: The granary keeper's hoard
granary_hoard.text: The keeper of the royal granary at {place} has been selling the crown's grain at night to merchants across the border.

choices.label: Hang him over the granary door
Take back what he made and dismiss him

harvest_gate.title: Women bar the gate to the recruiters
harvest_gate.text: The recruiters came to {place} for the seasonal levy in the middle of the harvest. The women have barred the gate and say the men can go when the grain is in.

choices.label: Take the men anyway
Wait until the harvest is in
Take every second man

militia_brawl.title: Militia brawl at the drill
militia_brawl.text: Two villages drilling together at {place} came to blows over an old boundary stone. A man is dead and both villages want the other punished.

choices.label: Hang the killer and end it
Make both villages pay blood money
Move the boundary stone to settle it for good

every_man_cripple.title: The lame and the old called up
every_man_cripple.text: Under the law that makes every man a soldier, the recruiters at {place} have taken a lame cobbler and a man of sixty. The town laughs at the crown's army.

choices.label: Every man means every man
Send them home and flog the recruiter

veterans_land.title: Veterans want their land
veterans_land.text: Old soldiers of the standing companies gather at {place}. They were promised land when they mustered out, and they have not had it.

choices.label: Grant them crown land
Pay them off
Refuse them

veterans_bandits.title: The veterans have taken to the road
veterans_bandits.text: The veterans the crown turned away have become a band on the roads near {place}. They know every trick the crown's soldiers know.

choices.label: Send the companies after them
Offer them their land after all

academy_duel.title: A duel at the academy
academy_duel.text: Two cadets of the military academy fought a duel over a woman at {place}. One is dead. He was {lord}'s nephew.

choices.label: Hang the survivor
Expel him from the academy
Call it honour and let it lie

knights_tourney.title: Knights brawl at the tournament
knights_tourney.text: The royal knights turned the tournament at {place} into a brawl with the townsmen. Three burghers lie dead in the lists.

choices.label: Strip the ringleaders of their spurs
Pay the widows and say nothing
Blame the townsmen

dwarf_guild_seat.title: Dwarves ask for a guild seat
dwarf_guild_seat.text: Under the charter, the dwarven smiths of {place} ask for a seat on the smiths' guild. The guildsmen threaten to close their stalls if one is granted.

choices.label: Grant them the seat
Refuse. The charter grants no seat

elf_grove_return.title: Elves ask to return to a grove
elf_grove_return.text: Elves of {place} ask to tend an old grove their grandfathers were driven from. A human farmer has ploughed half of it.

choices.label: Return the grove and pay the farmer
The farmer keeps his land

licensed_mage_fire.title: A licensed mage burns a barn
licensed_mage_fire.text: A mage licensed by the crown at {place} lost control of a spell and burned a barn with a family's winter stores in it. The Fire's priests are already preaching.

choices.label: Make the mage pay twice over
Revoke the licence and banish the mage
Protect the mage and pay the family

inquisition_lady.title: The Fire accuses a lady
inquisition_lady.text: The inquisition accuses {lord}'s wife of witchcraft. Her servants say she reads the stars; her accusers say she curdles milk. {lord} begs the crown to stop it.

choices.label: Let the trial proceed
Forbid it
Quietly send her abroad

restrictions_quarter.title: Non-humans driven from a quarter
restrictions_quarter.text: Under the restrictions, a mob has driven the non-humans of {place} out of their quarter and moved into their houses.

choices.label: Let the mob keep what it took
Restore the houses to their owners

faith_crown_rival.title: The crown's faith and the others
faith_crown_rival.text: Since the crown named its faith, the priests of the others at {place} say their temples are being taxed and their festivals refused. They ask for the same treatment as before.

choices.label: Grant it. The crown's faith needs no favours
Refuse. The crown has chosen

fire_bonfire.title: The Fire burns books
fire_bonfire.text: The Eternal Fire has lit a bonfire of books in the square at {place}, and among them are the town's own ledgers and charters.

choices.label: Let the fire burn
Arrest the priest who lit it

melitele_scoiatael.title: Priestesses shelter a wounded elf
melitele_scoiatael.text: The priestesses of Melitele at {place} are nursing a wounded Scoia'tael. They say the Mother turns no one away. The watch wants him hanged.

choices.label: Hang him when he can stand
Let the Mother keep him
Question him, then let him go

druid_curse.title: A druid curses the woodcutters
druid_curse.text: A druid has cursed {lord}'s men for felling a sacred grove near {place}. Two of them have since taken fever, and now no one will cut wood there.

choices.label: Spare the grove
Burn the grove and arrest the druid

lords_mill_quarrel.title: Two lords and one mill
lords_mill_quarrel.text: {lord} and a neighbouring house both claim the mill on their border near {place}. Both have sent armed men to sit in it.

choices.label: Give it to {lord}
Split the takings
Take the mill for the crown

lord_heir_debts.title: A lord's heir in debt
lord_heir_debts.text: {lord}'s heir has run up debts at the dice tables of Vizima that the house cannot pay. The creditors ask the crown to seize his horses.

choices.label: Pay the debts quietly
Let the creditors have their due

winter_wolves.title: Wolves at the walls
winter_wolves.text: The winter is hard. Wolves have come down to {place} and taken children from the edge of the village. The folk want a hunt.

choices.label: Pay a bounty for every pelt
Send soldiers to hunt
They must fend for themselves

spring_flood_debt.title: Flooded fields and the rent
spring_flood_debt.text: The spring floods have drowned the fields around {place}. The tenants cannot pay this year's rent, and the steward wants to evict them.

choices.label: Forgive the year's rent
Evict them

harvest_festival.title: A harvest festival
harvest_festival.text: The harvest is in at {place}, the best in years. The town asks the crown to send something for the festival.

choices.label: Send wine and a royal herald
Send congratulations and a tax collector

summer_drought.title: The wells run dry
summer_drought.text: A hot, dry summer. The wells of {place} are failing and the folk say the miller upstream has dammed the stream for his pond.

choices.label: Break the miller's dam
Make the miller sell water at a fair price

war_traitor_gate.title: An offer to open a gate
war_traitor_gate.text: A burgher of an enemy town has sent word through a merchant at {place}: for a purse of gold he will open a postern gate on a night of the crown's choosing.

choices.label: Pay him
It is a trap. Refuse

war_widows.title: The war widows
war_widows.text: The widows of {place} have walked to Vizima with their children. Their men died in the crown's war and the harvest will not come in without them.

choices.label: Grant each a widow's purse
Send them home with bread
Turn them away

war_deserter_son.title: A deserter in the family
war_deserter_son.text: {lord}'s youngest son deserted the army before the last battle. The soldiers want him hanged like any other deserter.

choices.label: Hang him like any other
Send him to a monastery

unrest_agitator.title: An agitator in the square
unrest_agitator.text: A preacher of no faith in particular is telling the crowds at {place} that the crown has forgotten them. Every day the crowd is larger.

choices.label: Arrest him
Invite him to court to speak
Let him talk. Talk is cheap

fear_informers.title: Informers everywhere
fear_informers.text: Neighbours in {place} are denouncing each other to the watch to settle old scores. The gaols are full of men accused of nothing anyone can name.

choices.label: Empty the gaols
Reward the informers. It keeps them loyal

love_petition_saint.title: A king's portrait in the chapel
love_petition_saint.text: The folk of {place} have painted the king's likeness among the saints in their chapel. The priests are uneasy.

choices.label: Let it stay
Ask them, gently, to paint it over

bridge_toll.title: A toll on the king's road
bridge_toll.text: The burghers of {place} have put a toll on their bridge. Carters say it is robbery; the town says the bridge will fall without it.

choices.label: Let the toll stand
Abolish it and pay for the bridge
Take the toll for the crown

plague_rumour.title: Talk of plague
plague_rumour.text: A sailor died of a fever at {place}, and the talk in the taverns is of plague. The town wants the gates closed; the merchants want them open.

choices.label: Close the gates for a month
Keep them open. It was one sailor
Burn the sailor's lodging and keep the gates open

refugees_border.title: Refugees at the border
refugees_border.text: Families from across the border, burned out by war or famine, have gathered outside {place}. They ask to settle on the empty land by the river.

choices.label: Let them settle
Turn them back
Let the young men stay for the levy, send the rest on

pretender_letter.title: A letter from a pretender
pretender_letter.text: A man in Redania claims to be a bastard of the old king and writes to {lord} asking for support. {lord} has brought the letter to the crown, sealed.

choices.label: Reward {lord}'s honesty
Thank him, and watch him

tithe_quarrel.title: The priests want their tithe
tithe_quarrel.text: The temple at {place} says the crown's tax collectors take the grain before the priests can take their tithe. The priests have stopped saying prayers for the king.

choices.label: The temple takes its tithe first
The crown comes first

witcher_fee.title: A witcher wants paying
witcher_fee.text: A witcher killed the beast that haunted the road near {place}. The villagers clubbed together half his fee and say the crown should pay the rest.

choices.label: Pay him the rest
Refuse. It is the village's beast
Have him run out of the parish
